**My thinking:**

I am 60 years old and I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, just like my mother did. I have no schooling but I know this soil. My plot is about 4 mu — not big, but it is mine. I manage it mostly by myself now.

Around here, everybody grows wheat in winter and corn in summer on the same land. That is what my family has always done. I am not going to try something new at my age. The wheat feeds the family and I sell some. The corn I mostly sell.

For wheat seeds, I will go to the village supply shop and buy whatever improved variety the shopkeeper recommends — something like Jimai. I have used improved seeds for years, I know they do better than the old seeds. For corn I always buy hybrid seeds, Zhengdan 958 or whatever is in stock. The hybrid corn is much taller and heavier.

For fertilizer, I do what my neighbors do and what my husband taught me. I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting, then add some urea when the wheat is jointing. For corn I top-dress urea once when it is knee-high.

I irrigate from the groundwater pump we share with neighbors. Wheat needs water three times — before winter sets in, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. Corn I water twice if rain is short.

I spray herbicide on the wheat and maybe once for aphids in May. Corn just needs one herbicide spray after planting.

I use a rotary tiller before wheat planting but after I harvest the wheat in June, I plant corn directly into the stubble without tilling — saves time and the village cooperative machine does it fast.
